channel.title: Curated Travel Magazine
channel.description: Travel reporting, cultural heritage, and responsible exploration worldwide.

item.title: Tivoli Mérida Residences Revives a Historic Yucatán Mansion
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
On Mérida’s celebrated Paseo Montejo, a restored 1903 mansion will become the heart of a new residential hospitality experience. Tivoli Mérida Residences will introduce 69 branded residences in the Yucatán capital, with the historic Casona 333 serving as the property’s social center. Its original character will frame a collection of guest amenities, including a restaurant, boulangerie, bar and piano lounge, along with a garden and terrace designed for private gatherings. The project brings Tivoli’s Latin American expansion to one of Mexico’s most culturally distinctive cities.

The Curated Take

The appeal here is the balance between the independence of a residence and the atmosphere of a historic hotel. In a city where architecture, food and local culture are central to the experience, placing a restored mansion at the center of the property gives the development a meaningful sense of place.

item.title: Michelin Makes Its Australian Debut in South Australia, Recognizing 77 Restaurants
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The MICHELIN Guide has made its Australian debut with an inaugural selection devoted entirely to South Australia, placing Adelaide and its surrounding wine regions on the international culinary map. Announced October 14, 2026, the guide recognizes 77 restaurants across the state, including Magill Estate Restaurant, which earned Two MICHELIN Stars, and 10 restaurants awarded One Star. Another 16 received Bib Gourmand distinctions, while 50 were included in the MICHELIN Selected category. Among the notable restaurants are Restaurant Aptos, led by American chef Justin James and known for its 16-course tasting experience featuring native Australian ingredients, and Restaurant Botanic, set within Adelaide Botanic Garden. The recognition follows anonymous inspections and evaluates ingredient quality, cooking technique, flavor, culinary personality and consistency.

The Curated Take

A MICHELIN Guide debut can reshape how an international audience sees a destination. For South Australia, the recognition adds a compelling culinary dimension to a region already known for its wines, landscapes and distinctive local produce. It also gives travelers a new way to build an itinerary around Adelaide and the surrounding wine country, connecting memorable dining with the producers, places and regional character behind the food. Importantly, the selection spans fine dining and more accessible restaurants, offering a broader picture of South Australia’s evolving food culture.

item.title: The Wolseley Brings Its London Legacy to New York
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A storied New York clubhouse is preparing for a new chapter, this time as the first hotel from The Wolseley Hotels. Set inside the McKim, Mead & White-designed former Lambs Club on West 44th Street, The Wolseley Hotel New York will bring 77 guest rooms and suites to Midtown, alongside a reimagined wellness center and the brand’s first restaurant in the United States. The Wolseley Members Club will add another dimension to the address, with a private, all-day setting for dining, culture and conversation.

The Curated Take

New York has no shortage of luxury hotels, but a property with a historic gathering-place identity and an established restaurant heritage brings a different proposition. The combination of hotel, dining and private club could make this more than somewhere to stay between city engagements.

item.title: A New Way to Exchange Extraordinary Second Homes Arrives in France
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Infinity by Pacaso has launched in France, expanding its invitation-only home exchange community to a country whose appeal spans Parisian residences, Provençal estates and Côte d’Azur villas. The network connects owners of exceptional second homes, allowing them to make unused weeks available to other vetted members in exchange for stays across more than 70 destinations in over 10 countries. Members can arrange direct exchanges or earn credits by hosting guests, then use those credits toward stays elsewhere in the collection. Each property and homeowner is personally vetted, while Pacaso coordinates the exchange details alongside the homeowner’s existing property manager. The launch was marked by a private preview at a residence on rue des Beaux-Arts in Paris, introducing French second-home owners to a network that already includes destinations such as St. Barths, Tuscany, Verbier, New York and Napa Valley.

The Curated Take

Luxury travel is increasingly shaped by access, privacy and the ability to experience a destination through a home rather than a hotel. Infinity offers a different proposition for second-home owners: turning time when a property would otherwise sit empty into opportunities to stay in other exceptional residences around the world. Its invitation-only structure and personally vetted membership are central to the concept, while the growing network could make returning to favorite destinations, or discovering new ones, more personal and residential in character.

item.title: Waikoloa Beach Marriott Unveils a Refreshed Hawaiian Retreat on the Kohala Coast
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The Waikoloa Beach Marriott Resort & Spa is entering a new chapter following a comprehensive renovation of its 297 guestrooms and suites, completed in December 2025. Inspired by Hawaiʻi Island’s natural landscape, the refreshed accommodations pair coastal colors, warm wood finishes and organic textures with cultural details. The resort has also introduced the Beach House at Waikoloa, a private oceanfront villa enclave offering dedicated concierge service, daily breakfast at Harvest 19 Kitchen & Bar and access to the wider resort’s dining, amenities and cultural programming. At Harvest 19, locally sourced ingredients celebrate the island’s agricultural heritage and the farmers, ranchers, fishermen and artisans who shape its food culture. Set along Anaehoʻomalu Bay, the resort brings together beachfront relaxation, contemporary accommodations and a stronger connection to the character of the Kohala Coast.

The Curated Take

A meaningful resort renovation should do more than update interiors; it should give travelers a deeper sense of where they are. Waikoloa Beach Marriott’s enhancements bring together three important elements of contemporary luxury hospitality: a renewed sense of place, more private accommodation options and dining rooted in local producers. The Beach House adds a residential-style experience for guests seeking greater privacy without giving up resort amenities, while Harvest 19 offers a connection to Hawaiʻi Island’s agricultural and culinary identity.

item.title: This Famous Japanese Art Collective Is Coming to California
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Japanese art collective teamLab is bringing its immersive art experience to Anaheim, California, with plans for its first permanent U.S. museum at OCVIBE in 2030. The approximately 110,000-square-foot museum will feature interactive installations that respond to visitors, making people an active part of the artwork rather than simply observers. Designed by Smith-Clementi, the museum will be part of OCVIBE, a developing arts, entertainment, dining, and hospitality district near the Honda Center.

The Curated Take

For travelers who have experienced teamLab’s celebrated installations in Japan, this brings a new opportunity closer to home. For California, it adds a distinctive cultural attraction to a destination increasingly bringing art, entertainment, and hospitality together. The larger appeal is the chance to experience art as something immersive and participatory, not simply something viewed from a distance.

item.title: A New Winter Wellness Retreat Opens Beneath Japan’s Mount Iwate
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Set against the snow-covered landscape of northern Japan, Azuma Farm Koiwai is welcoming its first winter season with the introduction of natural hot springs and Forest Springs SPA treatments. Opening November 20, the mineral-rich waters are drawn from 1,000 meters underground and supplied directly to the private baths in all 24 guest villas and the property’s three forest sauna pavilions. Beginning December 1, guests can also experience personalized massage treatments inspired by nature and the Five Elements, including a signature ritual combining horsehair brushing, warm stones and hands-on massage. Winter experiences extend beyond the spa, with guided snowshoe walks through forests and pastures beneath Mount Iwate and access to skiing at nearby Appi Kogen.

The Curated Take

Japan’s onsen culture has long been central to the art of the winter retreat. Azuma Farm Koiwai brings that tradition into a private, nature-led setting, pairing the restorative appeal of natural hot springs with forest saunas, wellness treatments and outdoor exploration. It offers travelers a compelling reason to look beyond Japan’s familiar urban and resort destinations and discover the quieter winter landscapes of Tohoku.

item.title: Birkie West Brings a Midwest Nordic Skiing Tradition to Colorado
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The American Birkebeiner Ski Foundation is bringing its celebrated Nordic skiing tradition west with Birkie West, a new event at YMCA of the Rockies’ Snow Mountain Ranch in Granby, Colorado. Drawing on the legacy of the Wisconsin Birkie, the weekend will bring together recreational skiers, competitive athletes and the wider Nordic community, with SNØ Racing athletes participating in races, cheering on competitors and leading clinics. Organizers expect more than 500 racers and 750 spectators. Set across Snow Mountain Ranch’s 5,100 acres, the destination offers more than 80 kilometers of groomed Nordic trails, making the event an opportunity to experience Colorado’s mountain landscape through one of winter’s most enduring outdoor sports.

The Curated Take

Birkie West reflects the growing appeal of destination-based outdoor events that bring together competition, community and access to the natural landscape. For travelers, it offers another reason to explore Colorado beyond its downhill ski resorts, while introducing the camaraderie and traditions of Nordic skiing to a broader audience. The combination of a major sporting weekend, extensive trail network and mountain lodging makes Snow Mountain Ranch an appealing winter destination for both dedicated skiers and those curious about the sport.

item.title: A Town Kept by Hand: The Living Heritage of Historic Granville
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Along the Cumberland River, about an hour east of Nashville, Historic Granville offers a glimpse into Tennessee’s Appalachian heritage through a community that has chosen to keep its traditions close. Operated by approximately 200 volunteers, the small town invites visitors to explore its historic streets, beginning at the T.B. Sutton General Store and extending to an antique car museum, pioneer village, and collections devoted to local foodways and whiskey history. The Granville Artisan Events and Gallery celebrates traditional Appalachian crafts, hand-forged work, and pioneer art, while Aunt Bee’s Farmhouse Quilt Shop and Bakery offers fabrics, patterns, and hands-on instruction in quilting, basket weaving, and other traditional skills. The historic general store, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, retains much of its early twentieth-century character and remains a gathering place for lunch, conversation, and the weekly Sutton Ole Time Music Hour. With accommodations at Granville Bed & Breakfast and nearby Wildwood Resort & Marina, the town offers an opportunity to experience a side of Tennessee shaped by craftsmanship, music, and community stewardship.

The Curated Take

Granville’s distinction lies not simply in its preservation of historic buildings, but in the people who continue to give them purpose. The volunteers, artisans, musicians, and shopkeepers make heritage something practiced rather than displayed. In a travel landscape often focused on what is new, Granville offers a quieter kind of discovery: the chance to encounter traditions that remain part of everyday community life because people have chosen to carry them forward.

item.title: Movie Night Gets a Maldivian Makeover at Siyam World
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At Siyam World, even movie night comes with a little adventure. The Maldives resort has introduced JetCar Cinema, an experience that takes the traditional drive-in concept onto the lagoon. Guests cruise across the water in a JetCar before settling in to watch a film on a floating screen beneath the night sky, with drinks and popcorn included. Accommodating up to four guests per session, the experience adds another playful dimension to a resort already known for its floating waterpark, horse ranch and electric go-kart track. Whether planned as an unconventional date night or a memorable evening with family and friends, JetCar Cinema turns a familiar holiday pastime into something distinctly Maldivian.

The Curated Take

Luxury travel increasingly finds distinction in experiences that transform the ordinary into something memorable. JetCar Cinema is a lighthearted example of how resorts can use their natural setting to create activities that feel connected to the destination rather than interchangeable with experiences elsewhere. In the Maldives, where the lagoon is often the centerpiece of a stay, bringing the cinema onto the water gives guests another reason to enjoy it after sunset.
